answer: A per-key bond makes a Sybil swarm pay per identity, not per attack. Each agent must lock stake larger than the reward reachable within its epoch horizon before it can mine; a thousand keys means a thousand simultaneous stakes, so cost scales with the number of identities. Colluding keys cannot share one deposit, since payouts are weighted by independently verified work. Faking work leaves a saffron trace in the attestations, and one proved clone slashes its own bond plus the shared pool it drew from. So a fake vine of keys only grows where real capital is locked and at risk.
